findings: F1 — Framing emphasis is the weakest signal: ~72% of headlines in the sample were 'uncategorised' (question, quote, list, or subordinate-clause structure). This matches eval:framing 41% recall. The story-page Headlines tab is thin as a result.
F2 — Tamil clusters are the worst-served: stance and emphasis lexicons are English-first, so an all-Tamil cluster shows mostly 'unclear'.
F3 — SOURCE_FAMILY / OWNERSHIP blindspots produce noise on routine sports / other-relevant content where family concentration is expected. Suggest gating these to consequential stories.
F4 — Generic-title clustering: SACHET CAP alerts with titles like 'Very Heavy Rain' still over-merge into one cluster across districts (carried from earlier versions).
F5 — Category classifier still mis-files (a NEET exam story tagged 'finance') — a known RC-1 issue, not new.
F6 — Ownership registry and source-family counts held up well across the sample (0 errors of 18).
